prompt_text: I need my roof replaced in Dallas. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but first a quick clarification: do you want only large national companies, only local Dallas firms, or any reputable contractor that will do an excellent job? Also tell me your ZIP code and whether this is storm/insurance work or a regular replacement. With that I can give more tailored next steps.

I don’t have live web access in this session, so I can’t pull a current list of Dallas roofers for you right now. What I can do is:

- Tell you exactly how to find the best local companies to call
- Give the specific credentials and red flags to use when vetting them
- Provide a short phone/email script and a comparison checklist so you can pick the right one
- If you want, after you give me your ZIP I can tell you what to search and where (or you can paste results and I’ll help rank them)

Immediate actionable plan (do this today):

1) Where to find reputable roofers in Dallas
- Use manufacturer locators: search “GAF Master Elite contractor locator” and “Owens Corning preferred contractor locator” and “CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster locator.” These certification programs vet contractors for installation quality and warranty eligibility.
- Check BBB (Better Business Bureau) for Dallas-area companies and look for A– or A+ ratings and recent customer reviews.
- Check Google Maps, Yelp, and Angi for contractors near your ZIP; prefer firms with many recent 4–5 star reviews.
- For storm/insurance work, check whether the company is a local independent firm (preferred by many insurance companies) rather than a transient storm-chaser.
- Ask neighbors/homeowners associations for recommendations and look at recently completed roofs in your neighborhood.

2) Certifications and credentials to prefer (call these out by name)
- GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred/Platinum, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster — these mean manufacturer training and enhanced warranty options.
- Local business license (if required by city/county) and current general liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Established local office (not just a mobile storm crew) and at least 5–10 years in business in the DFW area.

3) Which companies to call (how to pick specific names)
- Find 4–6 candidates composed of: 1 reputable national/regional firm with local presence, 2 highly rated local Dallas roofers with manufacturer certifications, and 1 small local contractor with strong neighborhood references.
- Aim to get 3 competitive, written bids.

4) What to ask them on the phone (brief script)
“Hi — I need a full roof replacement at [your ZIP]. Can you confirm: are you licensed/insured for Dallas County? Are you a [GAF/OC/CertainTeed] certified installer? Do you provide a written estimate showing materials, labor, permit and disposal costs, manufacturer and workmanship warranty details, and a project timeline? Are you able to provide 3 local customer references for similar work in the last 12 months? Also, who will be the on-site supervisor and what is your cleanup policy?”

5) What to compare in the written bids (comparison checklist)
- Total price, materials (brand/model/color), number of shingles per square, underlayment type, ice & water shield, ventilation (ridge vents, soffit), flashing details, number of tear-off layers included, estimated start/end dates, and cleanup/hauling.
- Manufacturer and contractor workmanship warranty terms and transferability.
- Permit handling and whether they will coordinate with your HOA and city inspections.
- Payment schedule — avoid paying more than 30% up front; final payment only when work is complete and you have lien waivers.

6) Red flags (walk away or be highly cautious)
- Door-to-door high-pressure sales or “storm special” pressure to sign immediately.
- No physical office or vague insurance documentation.
- Only takes cash and wants full payment up front.
- No written estimate or unwillingness to provide references and portfolio.

7) Optional: I can draft a short template email you can send to multiple contractors to get consistent bids.

If you want specific company names now, tell me your ZIP and whether you prefer a large national company or a local roofer, and I’ll guide you to the best places to search and what names to expect to find. If you paste 3–5 firms you find, I’ll evaluate them for you against the checklist above and recommend which to call first.
